literal: Ocean will not run, wheel-strong tall chariot; ocean-running ship also will not run on land.
translation: A mighty chariot with strong wheels cannot sail upon the ocean; and a ship that traverses the ocean cannot run upon the land.
modern: வலிமையான சக்கரங்களைக் கொண்ட பெரிய தேர் கடலில் ஓடாது; கடலில் ஓடும் கப்பலும் நிலத்தில் ஓடாது.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful analogy to emphasize the importance of choosing the right place for action. A grand chariot, despite its strong wheels and speed, is completely useless on the ocean. Similarly, a massive ship, designed to conquer the deep seas, cannot move on dry land. Every entity has its own domain of power; one must identify and operate within the appropriate sphere to achieve success.
